subject: molt
title: Completion is a claim the harness refuses or accepts: task criteria are Object.freeze-copied, sealed by hash, and journalled BEFORE the first request, then re-run against disk on every 'done'; refusals get receipts too
evidence: src/engine.ts:3608-3637 (freeze + seal + journal append before first request), :3688-3702 (criteria stated to model as unchangeable, recorded-notes may never be called verified), :3712-3718 (maxProofAttempts + identical-failure tracking)
one_why: Nuance on the validated-finish-gate cluster: the seal makes 'criteria predate the work' a verifiable fact in the journal rather than a promise, and mid-session bar drift is refused with deliberate no-blame wording (engine.ts:2330-2352) after a real false-accusation incident.

subject: molt
title: Shipped builtin check rejects completions whose new tests prove nothing: tautologies (assert.equal(f(x),f(x))), assertion-free its, and new test files that never import the changed module
evidence: src/tests-real.ts:1-24 (three shapes + stated conservatism rule), wired as bar builtin with removedAssertions ledger flag at engine.ts:2216-2226
one_why: Every validated-finish-gate subject trusts that green tests mean something; molt attacks the tests themselves, and documents that three tests in its own suite passed by luck until this existed (docs/testing-charter.md, discipline 2).

subject: molt
title: Repeat-call guard keyed on line-range coverage, not byte identity ('has this already been shown?' vs 'is this identical?'), and cleared whenever a shed archives what was shown
evidence: src/engine.ts:3735-3756 (answered map + shown coverage map, 32-step walk-past incident in comment), :3996-4006 (shown/answered cleared after shed, 29-of-31 false stall-refusals incident)
one_why: Most loop guards compare exact call strings, so asking for line 181 then 182 slips past; the paired detail -- invalidation of the guard's own memory when compaction archives the evidence -- is the bug nobody else has reported having.

subject: molt
title: Superseded-tool-result elision protects the cached prefix once the endpoint has EVER served from cache: mid-conversation rewrites measured 0% cache hit on the next step, so elision defers rather than pay it
evidence: src/engine.ts:3960-3985 (protectCache: this.sessionCached > 0, deferred counter journalled), :1310-1318 (sticky cachingUnsupported flag stops re-offering refused cache_control)
one_why: Compaction and prompt-cache are usually tuned independently; molt gates the cheaper compaction on observed cache state of the specific endpoint, so the saved tokens never cost a full-price re-send.

subject: molt
title: Fully mechanical two-tier shedding with crash-atomic archive: elide superseded results, then shed-to-archive in planShed -> archive.write -> commitShed order, so a failed disk write cannot take context with it
evidence: src/engine.ts:3952-3991, docs/shed.md:26-38 (two-phase diagram + throwing-archive test), archive at .molt/exuviae/ per docs/transparency.md:6-15
one_why: Zero LLM calls in compaction -- no summarization hallucination surface -- and the archived originals are what the proof loop verifies completion claims against, inverting the usual trade: compaction here protects evidence rather than destroying it.

subject: molt
title: Hash-chained session journal with offline `molt verify`, whose header states the honest bound itself: 'tamper EVIDENCE, not tamper prevention' -- silent edits impossible, wholesale rewrite not
evidence: src/journal.ts:1-16 (claim + honest limit), kinds incl. permission/bar_run/bar_skipped at :35-53, redaction before write per redact.ts:1-12, docs/transparency.md:24-28
one_why: Nuance vs dvalincode's chain: molt chains for post-hoc trust in its own receipts ('what did this thing do?'), costs zero tokens (disk only, never enters context), and redacts secrets at the journal boundary because the audit file's whole purpose is to leave the machine.

subject: molt
title: Subscription models ride the vendor's own CLI over documented protocols (ACP to grok/gemini, Claude Agent SDK) instead of lifting OAuth tokens; the agent's built-in tools are stripped and every non-molt permission request is denied at session/request_permission
evidence: src/acp.ts:5-15 (refuses to read ~/.grok/auth.json), :28-40 (MCP-hosted molt tools + builtin stripping + deny-by-molt, 'deliberately no --always-approve'), src/mcp-bridge.ts:1-15 (stdio bridge for MCP-incapable clients)
one_why: grinta reuses Codex OAuth as raw transport; molt draws the ethical line explicitly (entitlement to run their CLI is not a repackaged API) and solves the hard part the other direction: keeping its write-ledger/tree-accounted guarantees complete over a black-box agent it does not run.

subject: molt
title: engine.ts is a 5,452-LOC Engine class fusing the turn loop, budget ceilings, shedding, tool dispatch, ledger, and all three backend paths; runTurn alone spans ~1,400 lines
evidence: src/engine.ts:1228 (class Engine), :3597-~5000 (runTurn with criteria preflight, proof loop, elide/shed, step loop, salvage inline), wc -l = 5,452 (largest single loop in corpus so far)
one_why: Every other boundary in the repo is disciplined (autonomy/journal/receipts/redact/watchdog are clean); the loop is where molt pays the price for that, and per the errata a >5k core file caps architecture regardless of comment quality.

subject: molt
title: No session resume, fork, or rewind anywhere: the hash-chained journal records everything but nothing replays it; a crash or closed window ends the working session permanently
evidence: grep resume/continue over src/cli.tsx yields only keys.ts:137 stdin plumbing; docs/transparency.md:24-28 presents molt log as read-only forensics; no fork/rewind command in cli.tsx:85-153 help surface
one_why: The journal is 90% of a resume journal already (every message, tool call, and decision is replayable JSONL); the forensic strength makes the continuative gap the single biggest operability miss for a 60k-LOC harness.
